clue.text: A concert is hosted by individual with assured confidence

indicators.note: the word individual hosts, that is holds inside it, the run of words before this phrase

parts.note: individual means one, a single person
a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: Someone single puts on a concert with total self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is hosted by' signals the container. 'concert' is the stock crossword prom. To be on a promise is to expect a reward confidently.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in that position is sure of getting a reward they have been promised, so they wait with assured confidence.

clue.text: Not roping off outer London area

indicators.note: off describes something gone bad or out of its normal state, so these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declines to rope off a district on the edge of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of NOT ROPING. Orpington is a suburb in south-east London, in the borough of Bromley.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpington is a town on the south-eastern edge of Greater London.

clue.text: Weight minimally up in a year, as well

indicators.note: in places the turned weight abbreviation inside the letters from a and year
in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: weight cut to its minimum is lb, the short form for a pound

explanation.surface: A tiny weight gain over a year, and good going too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals the reversal in this down clue, and 'in' the container. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something capably is doing it well; both are adverbs of skilful performance.

clue.text: Control and break cats and dogs, perhaps

parts.note: a break is a rest from work
heavy rain is said to be raining cats and dogs, so these animals hint at a downpour

explanation.surface: How to keep and handle pets that misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about pets; really 'cats and dogs' is the idiom 'raining cats and dogs'.
explanation.definitionFit: To control someone or something is to hold it back, keep it in check.

clue.text: Mother has extremely pernicious illness

parts.note: mum is an everyday word for mother

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, that is the first and last letters, of the word pernicious

explanation.surface: A mother is suffering from a dangerous disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'pernicious', P and S. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A viral infection that swells the glands of the neck, a common childhood illness.

clue.text: A crime, so to speak

parts.note: so to speak reads literally: a wrong committed by speaking, false and damaging words said aloud about someone

explanation.surface: Something is called a crime only loosely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' looks like a hedge that it is not quite a crime, but it says the offence is committed by speaking. Strictly it is a civil wrong in England, hence the hedge too.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoken form of defamation, damaging a reputation with false words.

clue.text: Christmas service with chant belted out around end of evening

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters sit round the final letter of evening
belted out suggests singing loudly, but here the words are knocked out of shape and rearranged
end of picks the last letter of the word evening

explanation.surface: A carol is sung loudly at a late-night Christmas church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belted out' rearranges WITH CHANT, and 'around' puts that round G, the end of 'evening'.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchnight is a late-night church service held on Christmas Eve or New Year's Eve.

clue.text: German town about to be surrounded by British soldiers

indicators.note: to be surrounded by means the word about goes inside the letters for British soldiers

parts.note: soldiers are men, the ordinary ranks
re means about, concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A German town is about to be encircled by British troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'nearly', but it is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bremen is a port city in northern Germany.

clue.text: Harvest stored in a farm building over in Greek site

indicators.note: stored in means the harvest word is kept inside the other letters, as grain is stored
over means the farm building word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a silo is a farm building for storing grain
a crop is a harvest

explanation.surface: Grain is stored in a farm building at an ancient Greek place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' signals the reversal and 'stored in' the container, with 'in' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis of Athens is the citadel holding the Parthenon, a famous ancient site in Greece.

clue.text: E.g. breakfast cereal

definitions.meaning: breakfast is an example of an eating occasion, like lunch or dinner
a ground grain, as in oatmeal or cornmeal

explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is one of the day's main eating occasions, and coarsely ground grain such as oatmeal is also called this.

clue.text: Small amount of money yours truly's invested in bond

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is put into something

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, one hundredth of a dollar
yours truly is the speaker, me; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A small sum of the writer's money is tied up in a financial bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly' is the setter, ME. 'invested' and 'bond' suggest finance, but bond is the definition, a binding material.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a substance that binds bricks or stones together, a bond.

clue.text: Campaigner less polite about South Africa

indicators.note: about means the word for less polite goes round the letters for South Africa

parts.note: cruder means ruder, less polite

explanation.surface: An activist is ruder than others when talking about South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; it does not mean 'regarding' here.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns energetically for a cause.

clue.text: Right annoyed with friend entering racing event

indicators.note: entering means the friend word goes inside, between the letters for right and annoyed

parts.note: cross means annoyed
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone is rightly annoyed when a friend enters a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the container, with 'with' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallycross is a motor sport with cars racing on a mixed tarmac and gravel circuit.

clue.text: Number in SF movie shown in New York

indicators.note: shown in means the movie and the word in are placed inside the New York letters, as a film is shown in a city

parts.note: E.T. is the famous science-fiction film by Spielberg

explanation.surface: A number appears in a sci-fi film screened in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' signals the container. The first 'in' looks like a link word but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a number, nine times ten.

clue.text: Mr. Yeltsin is out of order, banishing unknown musician

indicators.note: banishing means sending away, so the unknown letter is removed
out of order means the name's letters are jumbled, put in a new order

parts.note: in algebra an unknown is x, y or z; here Y

explanation.surface: A Russian president behaves badly and sends away a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' jumbles MRYELTSIN, and 'banishing' takes out Y, an unknown. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A minstrel was a medieval travelling musician and singer.

clue.text: Son inspires east Sri Lankan

parts.note: to inspire is to breathe in, inhale

explanation.surface: A son motivates someone from Sri Lanka's east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' looks like 'motivates' but has its literal sense, breathes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinhalese are the largest ethnic group of Sri Lanka, and this is their language.

clue.text: Hold steady view about former PM losing power

indicators.note: about means the view word goes round the shortened prime minister

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: losing means the letter for power is taken away from the prime minister's name

parts.note: Pitt, Elder or Younger, was a British Prime Minister
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A view of a former prime minister after he has lost power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' signals the deletion and 'about' the container. Both Pitts, Elder and Younger, were British prime ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay firmly put and not move or change your position is to hold steady.

clue.text: Great concert with no end of horseplay

parts.note: a gig is a concert, a live performance

indicators.note: with no end of means the last letter of the horseplay word is dropped

parts.note: antics are horseplay, silly behaviour

explanation.surface: A great concert with endless larking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no end of' drops S from ANTICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gigantic is huge, enormous, great in size.

clue.text: Humiliate worker? Charming

parts.note: to gall is to vex or humiliate
a worker ant, the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: Is embarrassing a labourer a nice thing to do?
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the worker ant.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant man is courteous and attentive, charming, especially towards women.

clue.text: Harm to reputation among people in court

parts.note: in means among, within a group
a jury is the panel of people who sit in court to give the verdict

explanation.surface: Someone's good name is damaged in front of a courtroom audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The law speaks of damage to a person's good name as an injury, which the definition names.
explanation.definitionFit: Injury is damage or harm, and in law that includes damage to one's good name.

clue.text: Released from Auntie Doreen's clutches

indicators.note: from her clutches means the letters are held in the grip of these two words
from her clutches means the letters are held in the grip of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from an aunt's tight grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from ... clutches' takes the run spanning aUNTIE Doreen.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied means freed of knots or ties, released.

clue.text: Barrier to legal reforms, given little time originally

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word time, its first letter
reforms means the letters are formed again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Legal reforms are blocked, given little time to pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges TO LEGAL with T, the original letter of 'time'; 'given little' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollgate is a barrier across a road where a charge must be paid to pass.

clue.text: We've heard cavalry regiment take regular snacks

indicators.note: we've heard means the word is spoken and the sound is what counts

parts.note: the Royal Scots Greys were a famous cavalry regiment, known as the Greys

explanation.surface: Rumour says a mounted regiment keeps nibbling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots Greys were a British cavalry regiment, said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze is to eat small amounts frequently throughout the day, as animals at pasture.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well beginning to stagger, gripped by drink

indicators.note: gripped by means the letter is held inside the drink word

parts.note: water is a drink

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word stagger

explanation.surface: A layabout starts to stagger with a drink in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives S, and 'gripped by' puts it inside WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A waster is an idle, good-for-nothing person, a layabout.

clue.text: Port I kept under the counter

indicators.note: kept under means that in this down entry, the I is placed below the counter word

parts.note: a bar is a counter in a pub

explanation.surface: Someone keeps something hidden under the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept under' places I under BAR in the down entry. Bari is a port in southern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bari is a port city on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: French writer fails to finish long story

indicators.note: fails to finish means the last letter of the writer's name is cut off

parts.note: Françoise Sagan was a French novelist, author of Bonjour Tristesse

explanation.surface: A French author can't complete a long tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' drops the N of SAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally a medieval Norse tale.

clue.text: Inelegant description of meal served by non-believers?

definitions.text: description of meal served by non-believers?
definitions.meaning: non-believers say no prayer of thanks before eating, so their meal is without one

explanation.surface: An awkward dinner hosted by atheists.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second definition as a description of a meal without the blessing said before it, as atheists would serve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy, lacking elegance; also literally a meal eaten without the prayer of thanks first.

clue.text: Twee sister turned out savvy, in a way

indicators.note: turned out means the letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A prim sister grew up worldly-wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like 'became' but signals the anagram of TWEE SISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being streetwise means having shrewd knowledge of city life, a kind of savvy.
